headline: Veeam Agent Named-Pipe Flaw Lets Local Users Become SYSTEM (CVE-2026-32996)
summary: A high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability in Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows allows low-privileged local users to gain SYSTEM privileges. The flaw is rated 7.3 (High) and is reportedly exploited in the wild with public PoC code.
details: CVE-2026-32996 is a high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability affecting Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows. It allows a low-privileged local user to exploit the product's endpoint backup service to execute commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, the highest local privilege level.
The flaw, rated 7.3 (High) under CVSS v4, is actively being exploited in the wild, with public proof-of-concept code now available. This makes immediate patching critical for affected systems.

The defect resides in the Veeam Endpoint Backup service's handling of elevated client sessions over a local gRPC named pipe. Elevated session UIDs, which are stored insecurely in a log file readable by standard users, can be replayed by an unprivileged process to inherit an elevated context.

Exploitation requires local access to an affected endpoint but does not require initial administrator rights. An attacker only needs to read the service log and access the named pipe to achieve SYSTEM privileges.

Successful exploitation grants an attacker full control, enabling them to disable security tools, install persistence, harvest credentials, and move laterally within the network. Compromised hosts may also expose backup repositories and stored recovery data.

Users are advised to upgrade to Veeam Backup & Replication 13.0.2.29 or later, which includes the fixed agent build 13.0.3.1220. If immediate patching is not feasible, restrict interactive local logon and limit local administrator and backup operator privileges to essential personnel, prioritizing shared servers and administrator workstations.

topic: Meta Muse AI likeness to OpenClaw
headline_marked: [[Meta confirms Muse is 'heavily inspired' by OpenClaw]], addressing user speculation
headline: Meta confirms Muse is 'heavily inspired' by OpenClaw, addressing user speculation
summary: Meta's head of product, Nat Friedman, confirmed the AI agent Muse took heavy inspiration from the open-source project OpenClaw, following viral user comparisons and claims of identical system files.
details: Early adopters of Meta's AI agent Muse speculated it was OpenClaw under the hood, wrapped in a consumer-friendly package. Meta's head of product at Superintelligence Labs, Nat Friedman, has now confirmed Muse was "definitely heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw."

Friedman clarified that Muse itself was "built from scratch." He stated that the team at Meta had admired OpenClaw and aimed to create "something like OpenClaw" that could be scaled to billions of people.

Given OpenClaw is an open-source project, Meta drawing inspiration is not surprising, especially after its breakout success. This move aligns with Meta's known strategy of adopting successful features from promising products, similar to its approach with Snapchat's stories format.

The official admission came after an X post by AI app co-founder Ansh Nanda went viral, claiming "Muse is LITERALLY OpenClaw for normies." Nanda's post included a conversation where Muse itself acknowledged its system files' similarity to OpenClaw was "a match."

The viral thread prompted other users to share their findings, including that Muse also contained a SOUL.md file. This plain text configuration file defines an AI agent's personality, communication style, and behavioral boundaries.

Further comparisons revealed that not only were the file names identical between the two assistants, but their content was also almost entirely the same. When questioned about the identical file names and content for SOUL.md, Friedman responded that "we thought that Peter [Steinberger, OpenClaw's creator] got those things exactly right."

Friedman elaborated on X, stating that after using OpenClaw in January, he bought hundreds of Mac minis for his team, and many "fell in love with using OpenClaw." He praised Peter Steinberger as a genius and his harness as pioneering.

Muse has seen significant success since its launch, recently hitting No. 1 on the U.S. App Store. Data suggests its launch performance is outpacing that of ChatGPT when comparing platforms and market availability.
A Meta spokesperson, when reached for comment, referred to Friedman's statement and indicated the company had nothing further to add.
